sentenceVerdicts.reason: Patient explicitly states dry, tickly cough for about three weeks.
Patient confirms the cough is worse at night.
Patient confirms breathing is fine, denying shortness of breath.
Patient confirms taking lisinopril every morning.
Patient hedges the dose stating 'I think it's the 20 mg or maybe 40'.
Clinician explicitly states blood pressure today is 138/88.
Patient reports home BP readings are mostly in the 130s.
Clinician notes cough is a known side effect of lisinopril.
Clinician instructs to stop the lisinopril.
Clinician prescribes losartan 50 mg once a day.
Clinician advises to keep cutting back on salt.
Clinician schedules follow-up BP check in four weeks.

checklist.explanation: The clinician communicated the in-office blood pressure measurement of 138/88.
Lisinopril was discussed, but the exact dose was uncertain and unconfirmed.
Clinician asked if lisinopril is taken every day, and patient confirmed every morning.
Patient brought up a cough, and clinician identified it as a medication side effect.
Allergies were not reviewed despite prescribing losartan.
Clinician scheduled follow-up in four weeks.
Home blood pressure monitoring and values were discussed.
Shortness of breath was asked, but other red flags like chest pain or headache were not covered.
Clinician discussed continuing to cut back on salt.
Alcohol and tobacco use were not addressed.
Kidney function or potassium labs were not reviewed or ordered despite switching ACEi to ARB.

checklist.itemId: open:match:Review basic metabolic panel (kidney function, potassium) after lisinopril start
checklist.explanation: BMP labs for kidney function and potassium were not discussed.
Home BP readings were verbally asked and discussed, but a formal log was not reviewed.
